correctness.rationale: All n>=2, 1<=k<=floor(n/2) and W>0: the star Laplacian invariant splitting isolates n-1 leaf-zero-sum eigenvalues. Added weighted-edge matrix is positive semidefinite with rank<=k and trace 2T. A sharp Jensen inequality yields the bound; equality of Gram matrix eigenvalues forces k equal weights and zero off-diagonal edge-incidence products, hence a matching. Strong concavity and the exact Gram-square expansion give the quantitative penalty. Actual NumPy script checked 14,107 finite cases and the bound, which supplements but does not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: Actual semantic database queries and accessible prior-record claims did not show this exact two-budget star theorem. Primary full-text comparison distinguishes fixed-weight topology selection (Summers et al., 2014), continuous optimization on a fixed topology (Ghosh et al., 2008), general unweighted NP-hardness (Kooij–Achterberg, 2023) and general weighted mixed-integer relaxation (Bhoite et al., 2026) from the proved analytical closed form, all-minimizer matching rigidity, and nonzero overlap/imbalance penalty. Unindexed specialized prior results remain possible, not ruled out by a failed search.
residual_risks: Targeted searches cannot rule out an unindexed star-specific effective-resistance design theorem or a simple previously published consequence of a stronger spectral majorization result.
The 2026 general-budget preprint was inspected for relevant statements but not verified line by line in every ancillary appendix; concealed coverage of this instance is possible.
A restricted unweighted version could appear as a known matching extremal for graphs formed by adding edges to a star; this exact continuous-budget plus quantitative-rigidity result was not found.

value.rationale: The known network-coherence improvement problem jointly involves discrete topology and continuous reinforcement cost. A sharp, full-family closed solution on the natural hub-and-spoke base identifies disjoint links as optimal and quantifies the exact cost of physical link concentration or weight unevenness. This is a structural and resource-allocation boundary, not a mere numerical benchmark or renaming of a standard convex fixed-topology calculation.
